hook: An AI agent that reads firmware failure evidence like a senior engineer — and shows its work.

problem.statementExec: Before a firmware build ships, it runs through huge automated test suites — and a meaningful number of tests fail. Every failure used to need a senior engineer to read the evidence and write the verdict. The bottleneck was never the tests. It was the handful of people who can read a trace.
problem.statementTech: Manual failure analysis means reading multiple log formats and binary traces, decoding internal event and stop codes, cross-referencing firmware source at the exact build under test, applying tribal knowledge about subsystem ownership, searching the tracker for duplicates, then deciding root cause, classification, owner — and writing a structured report. Hours of expert time per failure, with FA capacity scaling with headcount while test volume scales with compute.
painPoints: Hours of scarce expert time consumed per failure
Tribal knowledge locked in a few senior heads
marginNotes: three architecture generations, each forced by a measured failure
~15 governed pipeline stages · verdict frozen before precedent search
source read at the pinned build, never current HEAD

approach.summaryExec: We made the agent the analyst: senior engineers' procedure became versioned skills, mechanical work stayed deterministic, and the whole pipeline is governed by a state machine so quality never depends on the model choosing to behave.

stages.label: Prepare
stages.captionExec: Evidence is gathered and fixed in place before any reasoning starts.
stages.captionTech: Case preparation hashes the evidence set and pins source revisions — everything later reads via immutable object access.

stages.label: Investigate
stages.captionExec: The agent reads the logs, then the source — with the access it needs, and nothing more.
stages.captionTech: State-machine stages scope tool access per phase: log investigation sees case artifacts only; source investigation gets read-only approved repos at the pinned revision.

stages.label: Synthesise
stages.captionExec: Findings are assembled into a causal picture, with every claim tied to evidence.
stages.captionTech: Evidence validation runs deterministic citation and entailment checks; a causal graph is built with edge admissibility verified in code.

stages.label: Classify
stages.captionExec: Candidate categories are scored blind, so the model can't anchor on a front-runner.
stages.captionTech: All five classification lanes are evaluated without revealing the current leader; severity is derived from structured fields, never argued in prose; confidence is adjudicated before validation.

stages.label: Precedent
stages.captionExec: Only after reaching its own verdict may the agent look at past cases.
stages.captionTech: Duplicate search runs behind a lock gate whose integrity re-verifies; it may identify duplicates but never revise the frozen conclusion.

stages.label: Report
stages.captionExec: A structured report — or an honest 'unresolved', never a confident guess.
stages.captionTech: Schema-validated rendering from a single format source; low confidence completes as a labelled unlocked report — abstention is a first-class output.

engine.evaluation: Model-as-judge scoring against senior-engineer ground truth on a golden set across seven verticals; model migrations run as formal A/B UAT against the production baseline. A gated skill-optimisation loop promotes a revision only when it strictly beats the incumbent on held-out cases.

value.before: Every failure queued behind a senior engineer: hours of expert reading per case, inconsistent verdicts, and knowledge that lived in people's heads instead of in testable artifacts.
value.after: Unattended triage for the recurring cases, with precedent cited, uncertainty labelled, and only genuinely novel failures escalated — plus the experts' procedure captured as versioned, testable skills.

metrics.label: verdict reached before precedent is consulted
low confidence completes as a labelled report

inputs.label: Test failures needing analysis per week
Share of cases solvable without escalation

roi.formula: hours = failures * share * mins / 60 * 4.33; value = hours * rate
roi.footnote: Illustrative estimate based on outcomes observed in comparable engagements. Not a quote.
